title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR 1 — velle / nolle
pass_a_gloss: GAR. For indeed 1. those things are not one and the same, of which a man can at the same time will the one and not-will the other. But so it stands in this case. For Adam, eating of the forbidden fruit, was willing to violate God's precept, but was unwilling to lose his justice and prerogatives.
pass_b_english: Garissoles' first reason. Things are not one and the same if a man can at once will the one and refuse the other. So here: Adam, eating the forbidden fruit, meant to break God's command, yet did not mean to lose his righteousness and privileges.
source_text: GAR. Etenim 1. non unum idemque sunt, quorum unum idem homo eodem tempore velle potest, & alterum nolle. At ita habet in hac causa. Adamus enim de fructu interdicto comedens, volebat violare Dei praeceptum, sed nolebat justitiam suam & praerogativas amittere.

choices.choice: velle one / nolle other ⇒ not formally identical
choices.why: Opens three rationes against formal identity
